findings.evidence:
`pkg/ddl/modify_column.go:234` now prefers `model.FindColumnInfo(..., getRemovingObjName(args.OldColumnName.L))` when `args.OldColumnID == 0`, only falling back to the original name lookup.
`pkg/ddl/modify_column.go:1124` shows new modify-column jobs don’t initialize `OldColumnID`, so the first execution always enters this name-based path.
`pkg/parser/misc.go:24` includes `$` in `isIdentChar`, so identifiers like `_Tombstone$_a` are syntactically valid (and there’s no repo-wide guard/validation for this prefix; `_Tombstone$_` only appears as `pkg/ddl/executor.go:85`).
findings.fix:
Disambiguate the “old column by name” fallback:
- Prefer original-name lookup for early phases (e.g. `job.SchemaState != model.StatePublic`), and only prefer removing-name lookup when the job is expected to have already renamed the old column (e.g. `job.SchemaState == model.StatePublic`).
- Additionally/alternatively, when the removing-name lookup hits, require a non-`StatePublic` column (internal removing column) before accepting it; otherwise fall back to the original-name column.
findings.impact: If a table contains a user column named `_Tombstone$_<col>` (or a leftover internal tombstone column unrelated to the current job), `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN <col>` can pick the wrong `oldCol` on the first execution (when `OldColumnID` is still 0). This can lead to modifying the wrong column, DDL failure, or persisting inconsistent table metadata (e.g. duplicate column names) depending on the modify-column path.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `bab4993b6fd61de478062151bb615a0e09c0aecb`: `getModifyColumnInfo` still prefers removing-name lookup first when `OldColumnID` is missing (same risk remains).
findings.what: `getModifyColumnInfo` can misidentify the target column when `OldColumnID` is missing: it now looks up `_Tombstone$_<oldName>` before `<oldName>`, so tables that already contain a `_Tombstone$_<oldName>` column can cause `MODIFY COLUMN <oldName>` to operate on the wrong column.

subject: ddl: find old column by name for old version modify column job (#63901)
summary: Commit adds a compatibility fallback for old modify-column jobs missing `OldColumnID` by searching the removing-name (`_Tombstone$_<col>`) first, plus an integration test and minor refactors (reorg-timeout helper; defaulting/logging when certain session vars are absent; a test-only job-args mutator). One High-risk edge case remains: the removing-name-first lookup can mis-target user schemas that already contain `_Tombstone$_<col>` columns.
